dispositions.reason: Fixed, but still reported. Squisq pins every @tiptap package to 2.27.3, which backports the upstream fix: its only source change is the same __proto__ guard in mergeAttributes that 3.30.4 ships. npm still flags it because the advisory's affected range (<3.30.4) does not credit the 2.x backport.
dispositions.remediation: Nothing to renew. The verification test fails the build if an unpatched @tiptap/core is ever installed. When the advisory is corrected and npm stops reporting it, the audit gate notes that this entry can be deleted.

dispositions.reason: Only inside the pinned npm 11.19.1 toolchain, which bundles brace-expansion@5.0.9 (brace-expansion: DoS via uncontrolled recursion in parseCommaParts causing stack exhaustion). npm installs dependencies on developer and CI machines and is not part of any DocBlocks artifact; every application copy of this package is already on a fixed version. No npm release bundles the fix yet: 11.20.0 and 11.21.0 still ship the same version.
dispositions.remediation: Move the pinned npm (package.json devDependencies, engines and packageManager, checked by check:dependency-governance) to the first release that bundles brace-expansion 5.0.12 or later, then delete this entry.

dispositions.reason: braces@3.0.3 has no patched release. Build and release tools still use it through micromatch. Desktop now uses Chokidar 4.0.3, which has no glob dependencies, and electron-builder excludes braces, micromatch and fast-glob from Gezel's unused full-service file-search implementation. DocBlocks hosts only Gezel's inference-only profile. The packaged smoke suite verifies the excluded packages are absent from app.asar and that hosted AI still starts.
dispositions.remediation: Move the remaining tooling consumers to a fixed braces release once one exists and passes the seven-day cooldown, or replace their glob implementation. Retain the desktop exclusions until the complete audit and packaged AI smoke prove that restoring these packages is safe.

dispositions.reason: http-cache-semantics@4.2.0 has no patched release. The exact dependency paths are electron-builder -> app-builder-lib -> @electron/get -> got -> cacheable-request, and the pinned npm 11.19.1 -> make-fetch-happen. Both run only on developer and CI machines; neither HTTP cache implementation is included in any DocBlocks distribution.
dispositions.remediation: Update the electron-builder dependency closure and pinned npm to releases containing a fixed http-cache-semantics once a patch exists and the seven-day cooldown has elapsed, then remove this entry.
